papers.relied_on: Score entries assumed the review supports insulin (+/- C-peptide) and glucose at nadir or in a mixed-meal test to confirm hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia and exclude insulinoma and drugs; row 5 and U4/U5 note 'full text empty'.
papers.full_text_shows: Full text is available. The proposed diagnostic criteria are history, venous glucose below 54 mg/dL with neuroglycopenia relieved by treatment, and no hypoglycaemia after a 12-hour fast; insulin is not among them. Insulin or beta-cell peptide testing at symptomatic hypoglycaemia is described as used 'by those with access to endocrine testing centers' with no normative data; research shows insulin not fully suppressed at glucose below 50 mg/dL. The mixed-meal test has no accepted standard (40 to 75 g carbohydrate), the liquid meal is contested, an oral GTT should play no role, and provocation risks severe hypoglycaemia. C-peptide is not mentioned. CGM should not be used for diagnosis. Insulinoma is excluded by inpatient fasting (fasting hypoglycaemia, onset under 6 months, atypical features), not by post-meal insulin. Authors disclose industry ties (Novo Nordisk, Xeris and others).
papers.quote: there are no normative data in this situation
papers.key_numbers: Strict definition: neuroglycopenia with plasma glucose below 50 mg/dL; diagnostic criterion venous glucose below 54 mg/dL; symptoms 1 to 3 h after meals; onset more than 1 year after surgery; 10% of healthy people have glucose below 50 mg/dL within 180 min of an OGTT; fast of at least 12 hours
papers.role_in_work: Main source for row 5 (post-bariatric hypoglycaemia) across U1 to U5 and S1.

papers.assay_or_platform: Not specified; refers to insulin above the lower limit of the assay used
papers.quality_note: Expert review, not a guideline; low-quality evidence; authors state divergence of opinion on the liquid meal.

proposals.reason: Entries assumed insulin at nadir supports the diagnosis and excludes insulinoma and drugs. The review's diagnostic criteria use history, glucose below 54 mg/dL with symptom relief and a 12-hour fast, with no insulin; insulin testing is described as used in endocrine testing centers without normative data; insulinoma exclusion is by inpatient fasting. Under clarification 15 the post-meal insulin neither determines the diagnosis nor is needed to support it. U4 and U5 already say management starts from glucose alone. Weak case: a fasting-test insulin (a different measure) would keep 2.
proposals.quote: documented hypoglycemia (venous glucose <54 mg/dL) at time of neuroglycopenic symptoms

proposals.reason: U2 scored D8 as useful in a defined subgroup (atypical cases). The full text sends atypical cases (fasting hypoglycaemia, onset under 6 months) to a prolonged inpatient fast and imaging, not to a post-meal insulin; glucose plus history defines the syndrome and there are no normative insulin data. No added value over glucose is shown for post-meal insulin, so 1 (marginal); 'not determinable' would also be defensible.
proposals.quote: there are no normative data in this situation

claim_issues.issue: Says Salehi 2018 full text is empty; a good full text is stored (PMC6692713). The test column lists C-peptide, but the review never mentions C-peptide.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Salehi 2018, PMID 30101281, DOI 10.1210/jc.2018-00528, full text (expert review, not a guideline). Insulin testing at symptomatic hypoglycaemia is described as used in endocrine testing centers; the review's diagnostic criteria do not include insulin; C-peptide is not mentioned.

claim_issues.issue: 'Confirm postprandial hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia; exclude insulinoma, drugs, exogenous insulin' is not supported by this paper: confirmation is by glucose and symptoms, insulinoma exclusion is by prolonged fast, exogenous insulin is not discussed.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Salehi 2018 documents hypoglycaemia by venous glucose below 54 mg/dL with neuroglycopenia. Insulin was not fully suppressed during hypoglycaemia in research studies, but the review gives no normative values and does not list insulin in its diagnostic criteria. Solid and liquid mixed meals are both used with no accepted standard; an oral glucose load should play no role.

claim_issues.issue: Salehi says blinded CGM may show patterns but should not be used for diagnostic purposes; the 54.3% CGM figure is from Lupoli 2021, not Salehi.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Salehi 2018 says CGM is less accurate in the hypoglycaemic range and should not be used for diagnosis; the 54.3% CGM prevalence is from Lupoli 2021.

claim_issues.issue: 'Meta-analysis ... shows improvement in insulin/HOMA-IR' omits that with pegvisomant plus somatostatin ligands only fasting insulin improved; it is a second-hand report.
claim_issues.proposed_wording: Pituitary Society 2021 cites a meta-analysis of 13 prospective studies (435 patients): fasting insulin and HOMA-IR improved with pegvisomant monotherapy; only fasting insulin improved when combined with somatostatin ligands.
